Meson Enquirer is a Discord bot for a Meson support server.
When someone opens a ticket and puts a swap ID, a transaction hash or an explorer link into the Ticket Tool form, the bot looks the swap up and posts the details straight into the ticket:

- status — always the same one the Meson explorer shows (pending / releasing / done / cancelled / expired, …)
- from chain and sender address, to chain and recipient address
- amount sent → amount received, with tokens
- one transaction hash per step (executed, releasing / released, cancelled, …), each linked to the right chain's explorer
- request time, and the Meson explorer link

It then follows the swap: the details update themselves as the status changes, a reply tells the user it is being processed (or, if it runs into trouble, that the funds are safe and support will look into it), and the user gets a **✅ Transaction Completed** or **↩️ Transaction Cancelled** message when it finishes.

If the ticket has only a wallet address, the bot lists that wallet's recent swaps that are **not** finished (done, released or cancelled). A wallet that has never used Meson gets no reply, because the server also supports other projects.

In those same ticket channels, anyone can also run `/meson-query` with a swap ID, source/destination hash or explorer link to see one swap's details. To limit who can use it, go to **Server Settings → Integrations → (the bot)**.

No API key is needed — the Meson endpoints it uses are public.

## Running it

Needs **Node.js 20.10 or newer**, [pm2](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/) to keep it running, and [Ticket Tool](https://tickettool.xyz/) for the tickets.

What this bot needs that is easy to miss:

- **MESSAGE CONTENT intent** (Developer Portal → Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents). Without it Ticket Tool's form arrives empty and the bot silently never replies.
- **Invite** with scopes `bot` + `applications.commands` and permissions **View Channel, Read Message History, Embed Links**. Leave out Send Messages here: the bot gets it only in ticket channels (through the category or the Ticket Tool panel), so it cannot post anywhere else.
- **Where it auto-replies:** only in channels (and their threads) under the `REPLY_CATEGORY_IDS` categories, and only where it has View Channel, Send Messages, Embed Links and Read Message History. Every other channel is ignored without looking anything up. In a private category, add the bot's role as a support role on the Ticket Tool panel — ticket channels get the panel's permissions, not the category's.
- `/meson-query` works only in the same `REPLY_CATEGORY_IDS` channels; anywhere else it answers with a private "can only be used in support ticket channels".

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env               # then fill in BOT_TOKEN, APPLICATION_ID, GUILD_ID, REPLY_CATEGORY_IDS, STAFF_ROLE_IDS
npm run register                   # once, and again after changing a slash command
pm2 start ecosystem.config.cjs     # runs it as "meson-bot"; then: pm2 save
```

`pm2 restart meson-bot` after changing code or `.env`; `pm2 logs meson-bot` to watch it.
To start it on boot: `pm2 startup` on Linux/macOS; on Windows (where that is not supported) a scheduled task that runs `pm2 resurrect` at login.

## Settings

Every setting is a line in `.env` and only there — the code has no defaults, and the bot refuses to start (naming the line) if one is missing or invalid.
After editing, `pm2 restart meson-bot`.
IDs: turn on Developer Mode in Discord, then right-click the server / role → Copy ID.

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `BOT_TOKEN` | The bot's login. Never share it. |
| `APPLICATION_ID` | Needed by `npm run register`. |
| `GUILD_ID` | Your server: `/meson-query` is registered there and appears at once. Blank = all servers, which can take up to an hour. |
| `REPLY_CATEGORY_IDS` | The ticket categories, comma separated. The bot auto-replies only in channels under them (and threads in those channels). Right-click a category → Copy ID. `/meson-query` is limited to the same channels. |
| `STAFF_ROLE_IDS` | Members with any of these roles are ignored, so IDs staff paste while investigating are not looked up. (Who may use `/meson-query` is set in Discord: Server Settings → Integrations.) |
| `AUTO_SCAN_MESSAGES` | How many messages from other bots (Ticket Tool's form) are read at the start of a ticket. The user's own messages are read for the whole ticket. |

**Wallet address lookups** — a ticket with only a wallet address gets that wallet's swaps that are not finished (done, released or cancelled). Meson cannot filter by status, so the bot reads newest-first, 20 per page, and stops at whichever limit comes first:

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `ADDRESS_LOOKBACK_DAYS` | Stop at swaps older than this many days. |
| `ADDRESS_MAX_PAGES` | Stop after this many pages (10 = the newest 200 swaps). |

**Following a swap until it finishes** — checks slow down the longer a swap stays unfinished. All swaps that are due, across every ticket, are checked together in one request (up to 20 per request), so more open tickets do not mean more requests:

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `SWAP_WATCH_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | Check this often at first — also how often the shared check round runs. `0` = don't follow swaps (no ⏳ or 🔎 line, and the closing note is only posted if the swap was already finished). |
| `SWAP_WATCH_SLOWER_AFTER_MINUTES` / `SWAP_WATCH_SLOWER_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | From this many minutes after the swap was requested, check this often instead (so a swap already old when its ticket opens starts on the slower checks). |
| `SWAP_WATCH_SLOWEST_AFTER_MINUTES` / `SWAP_WATCH_SLOWEST_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | From this many minutes (not less than the line above), check this often. |
| `SWAP_WATCH_LONG_AFTER_HOURS` / `SWAP_WATCH_LONG_INTERVAL_MINUTES` | Once a swap is this old (since it was requested), check it only this often. A swap is never dropped: it is followed until it finishes or its ticket is closed, so a late fix by the team still reaches the user. |
| `SWAP_WATCH_BUNDLE` | `true` = check every followed swap together: whenever the bot asks Meson about the swaps that are due, the others come along in the spare places of that same request (up to 20 per request, so never an extra request) — an old swap's completion is then posted as quickly as the newest swap is checked. `false` = each swap only at its own interval above. |
| `RELEASING_STUCK_AFTER_MINUTES` | A swap still "Releasing" this long after its deadline counts as stuck: its ⏳ "completed shortly" reply changes to 🔎 "taking longer than usual", which says the funds are safe and our support team will look into it. `0` = never. |

**When Meson's site is down** — it sometimes serves an error page for a moment:

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `MESON_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Give up on one request after this long. |
| `MESON_RETRIES` | Retry a failed request this many times, waiting about 1s, 2s, 4s, … between tries. |
| `TICKET_RETRY_SECONDS` / `TICKET_RETRY_MAX_SECONDS` | If it still fails, handle the whole ticket message again until it works — it never gives up while the ticket is open (only if Discord refuses the bot's post, e.g. missing permissions, since retrying can't fix that). The first retry waits `TICKET_RETRY_SECONDS`, each later one twice as long, never more than `TICKET_RETRY_MAX_SECONDS`. The same applies to rebuilding a ticket after a restart. |

**Network notice** — an unfinished swap's details show "⚠️ Network notice" while Meson reports its source or destination chain as unreachable (none of Meson's nodes for that chain healthy, per `rpcs.meson.fi`); it disappears on the next check once the chain recovers:

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `CHAIN_HEALTH_CACHE_SECONDS` | Re-check chain health at most this often (one request covers every chain). `0` = no notices. |

**Explorer status check** — the bot's statuses are a copy of the Meson explorer's own status function; this checks that Meson has not changed it:

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `EXPLORER_CHECK_HOURS` | Check at startup and every this many hours; a change is logged as a warning (`pm2 logs meson-bot`). `0` = never. Check by hand with `npm run check-explorer`. |

**New chains and tokens** — the bot reads Meson's own live table, so ones Meson adds are named correctly without a code change or restart:

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `PRESETS_REFRESH_HOURS` | Read the table at startup and every this many hours. A swap using an unknown chain or token also triggers a read straight away. `0` = only that straight-away read. |

**Random spacing** — so checks don't arrive at a fixed beat:

| Setting | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `JITTER_PERCENT` | Every wait above (check rounds, swap re-checks, retries) is made randomly up to this many percent shorter or longer — `50` turns a 10s check into anything from 5s to 15s, averaging the same rate. `0` = exact intervals. At most 90. |

## Checking it works without Discord

```bash
npm run lookup -- 0x1f399b606262b630e544f05cf09260f653ddc970aac581cc4c55d988a254a730
npm run lookup -- https://explorer.meson.fi/swap/0x1f399b60...
npm run lookup -- "my swap 0x047b1882... is stuck"

npm run lookup-address -- <wallet address>              # newest 10
npm run lookup-address -- <wallet address> 2            # page 2
npm run lookup-address -- <wallet address> --unfinished # what a ticket shows
```

Grab a real swap ID or address from <https://explorer.meson.fi>.

## What the user can paste

Anything the explorer's search resolves, alone or buried in a sentence, backticks or bold:

- the swap ID (`0x` + 64 hex) or the encoded swap
- the **source** or **destination** transaction hash (incl. Solana signatures and un-prefixed Tron/Bitcoin hashes)
- a Meson explorer link, or a chain explorer link (Etherscan, Solscan, Tronscan, mempool.space, …)
- a wallet address — used only when nothing above is found

Some chains' values look alike (a Sui hash looks like a Solana wallet, a Sui wallet like a swap ID), so the bot lets Meson's search decide what was pasted.

## Behaviour in a ticket

- **What is read:** Ticket Tool's form (the first `AUTO_SCAN_MESSAGES` bot messages) and every later message the user posts. Staff messages are ignored.
- **One embed per swap.** Each new swap gets its own details embed; the same swap again (its ID or either hash) is ignored. With several swaps, embeds are numbered #1, #2, …
- **Follow-ups**, as plain-text replies to the swap's embed (numbered "Swap #n" like the embeds when there are several):
  - ⏳ "being processed" while a swap is moving normally — deleted once the closing message is posted;
  - ✅ Transaction Completed / ↩️ Transaction Cancelled when it finishes — plus "this ticket will be closed soon" once every swap in the ticket is finished (if another swap is added later, the earlier messages get their "Swap #1" and lose "closed soon" for good — it goes on the closing message of whichever swap finishes last);
  - 🔎 instead of the ⏳ for Expired, Unlocked, Failed and stuck swaps (still Releasing well past their deadline), since "completed shortly" no longer holds: it says what is wrong, that the funds are safe and that our support team will look into it. A ⏳ already up is edited into the 🔎 (and back if the swap moves again); the bot keeps watching, and the ✅ / ↩️ replaces it once the team resolves the swap.
- **Status reason.** The details embed's description says what the current status means (for example "The funds have been received by the LP and are being released to the recipient."). `/meson-query` adds the support note there too, as it has no 🔎 reply.
- **Transaction hashes:** one entry per step, in process order, with the latest hash — failed attempts next to a successful one are not listed (they stay on the explorer); a step that has only failed so far is marked "(failed)". The release reads releasing → releasing (confirming) → released.
- **Live updates.** The details embed is edited in place as the status changes (timing: the `SWAP_WATCH_*` settings).
- **Network notice.** While a swap is unfinished and Meson can't reach its source or destination chain, the details embed says so ("⚠️ Network notice — Arbitrum is having network problems right now, which can delay this swap."). It goes away by itself once the chain is healthy again.
- **Wallet only.** If no swap is found and the ticket shows none yet, the bot lists the wallet's unfinished swaps (limits: the `ADDRESS_*` settings). If there are none it says so, and that it only checked Meson swaps. A wallet that has never used Meson gets no reply at all: the server also supports other projects whose forms ask for a wallet, and people do not always pick the right ticket category. A wallet pasted after a swap is shown is ignored.
- **No repeats.** A swap, wallet or unknown value pasted again gets no second reply in that ticket, also after a restart.
- **Not found.** If the user pastes something swap-shaped that Meson does not know, the bot says so, once per value (it still looks the value up each time, in case the swap has appeared since). The form never gets this reply — Ticket Tool embeds are full of Discord IDs and other hex-ish noise.
- **Meson's explorer down: limited details.** If the explorer can't be reached but Meson's relayer knows the swap, the ticket gets the details embed titled "Status unavailable (limited details)" — chains, amounts and the transactions found so far, but no status (the relayer cannot confirm one, so nothing ever says Done early), wallets or request time. The ⏳ / 🔎 / closing message wait until the explorer is back; then the embed is replaced with the normal one and the usual replies follow. A wallet address has no stand-in.
- **Meson down never loses a ticket.** If Meson can't be reached or rejects requests, the bot keeps retrying (the `TICKET_RETRY_*` settings) until the ticket is answered, and keeps following posted swaps through the outage. It stops only when the ticket is closed or Discord refuses the bot's post (e.g. missing permissions); a swap is followed until it finishes or its ticket is closed.
- **Restarts lose nothing.** On startup the bot reads every open ticket, rebuilds it from its own messages, carries on following each unfinished swap (updating the embed, changing ⏳ to 🔎, posting ✅ / ↩️ — including for swaps that became stuck or finished while it was down) and answers messages users sent while it was offline. It does the same after a long connection drop.
- **A failed post is tried again.** If Discord fails while the bot posts a ⏳, 🔎 or closing message, the next check tries again. If Discord refuses (e.g. missing permissions), it waits an hour between tries, and carries on once access returns.
- **New chains and tokens.** When Meson adds one, the bot picks up its name from Meson's live table, even if the swap is its first sight of it. If the table cannot be read at that moment, the embed shows `Unknown chain (0x…)` or `token#34` rather than a guess, and corrects itself once the table is read.

## Maintenance

New chains and tokens need nothing from you (see `PRESETS_REFRESH_HOURS`). To update the table the bot starts from, for example before a release:

```bash
npm run refresh-presets
```

It rebuilds `src/presets.json` from the live explorer. If any part cannot be read, or the table looks truncated, it fails and leaves the file as it was, rather than mislabelling swaps.

If `Unknown chain (0x…)` or `token#34` stays on a swap, look for `!! could not read Meson's chain and token table` in `pm2 logs meson-bot`: Meson may have changed their bundle layout, or their explorer may not know the chain yet.

## For developers

- `CLAUDE.md` — orientation: file map, "where to look for…", ticket flow, status table, rules to know before editing.
- `CONTEXT.md` — the Meson side: endpoints, the 32-byte encoded-swap layout, status meanings, and why the documented relayer API is only a stand-in.
- `CODE_INDEX.md`, each code file's "Contents" block and the section list at the top of long docs are generated line-accurate indexes, rebuilt before every `npm start` and after Claude Code edits a file. When editing by hand, keep `npm run index:watch` running.
- `npm run index -- --check` also checks the hand-written docs against the code (file map, settings, commands, npm scripts, links…) and fails on drift; Claude Code runs it automatically when it finishes a change.
- `npm test` runs the tests in `test/` against a fake Discord and a fake Meson, so it needs no `.env` or network. A fix or new behaviour gets a test that fails without it.
- `.env` is git-ignored (so is every `.env.*` except `.env.example`, which holds no token or IDs). Check `git status` before a first push.
